rationale: Lycopolitan/dialectal variant of ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become.' Recurs three times on this page (lines 1, 7, 8). The unusual orthography with ⲱⲟ̄ⲉ may reflect a scribal-orthographic feature of this manuscript witness. Confirmed by line 7 'the other man who became (ⲁϥϣⲱⲟ̄ⲉ) the companion of...'

proposed_english: to be sound / be healthy / be whole
rationale: Likely Lyc reflex of ⲟⲩⲟϫ 'be sound, whole, healthy' with regular ⲍ for ϫ. Circumstantial ⲉϥⲟⲩⲁⲍⲉ̄ 'while he is sound' fits the catechumen-soteriological register. Distinct from ⲟⲩⲱⲍ 'add' and ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'dwell.'

From verbal root ⲧⲗⲟ 'rejoice, give joy' (cf. ⲧⲉⲗⲏⲗ 'rejoice'). Substantival 'comfort/consolation.' Listed in lines 3 and 5 alongside prayers, psalms, and blessings as a good provided to the catechumen by his association with the elect community.

Hapax in this corpus. Object of habitual ⲕⲱ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forgive forth' construction in line 28; modified by ⲛⲟⲩⲙⲏⲏϣⲉ 'multitude.' Sense 'transgressions/faults' fits the forgiveness-of-sins context. Etymology unclear — possibly Lyc variant or scribal corruption.
Lyc reflex of Sah ϩⲙⲟⲧ 'gift, grace, favor' with regular ⲍ for ϩ (cf. ⲡϩⲙⲁⲧ already in accumulated vocabulary as same lexeme). The ⲍ-onset confirms Lyc orthographic register.

proposed_english: become a petitioner / become a supplicator
rationale: Verbal idiom ⲣ̄- + agent-noun ⲣⲉϥ-ⲥⲁⲡⲥⲡ ('one who supplicates,' from ⲥⲱⲡⲥⲡ̄ 'beseech, supplicate'). Captures the role-assumption: the Church habitually 'becomes-a-petitioner on your behalf' for the forgiveness of catechumens' sins. Standard Coptic agent-noun formation parallel to ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.'
